answer: Because the spiral count is verified against the zenith text itself, the fable audit records each rejection and the operator cannot amortise one paragraph. Filling 139 aliases thus means producing 139 separate sets of claims, which is authoring work rather than a lookup. An answer claiming a deep mechanism must supply at least 3 distinct supporting claims, and the count is checked before grading so shallow text cannot pass by padding. That is 23 dollars per alias. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
